hero.headline: Trump weighs Iran deal as negotiations continue
hero.body:
President Donald Trump met with his national security team to make a final determination on a potential agreement with Iran after weeks of diplomatic and military activity. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth discussed the ongoing negotiations publicly, though Trump has not yet announced a decision on whether to accept a deal.

The talks have created confusion about the administration's approach. Officials confirmed that the US and Iran have agreed on a framework for a deal, yet significant disagreements remain unresolved on critical points needed for any final accord.

Iran's negotiating team has cast doubt on the likelihood of an imminent agreement. Esmail Baghaei, Iran's foreign ministry spokesperson, stated that while progress has been made on many issues, "to say that this means the signing of an agreement is imminent, no one can make such a claim." He pointed to confusion in US positions and Israeli interference as obstacles to reaching an agreement.

Iran has insisted that a ceasefire in Lebanon must be included in any memorandum of understanding regarding the Strait of Hormuz, alongside US agreement to lift its blockade of Iranian ports. Baghaei also clarified that what the US characterizes as toll proposals for the strait are actually "fees for navigational services" to be negotiated between Oman and Iran.

By contrast, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio expressed optimism about prospects for a deal. Speaking during an official visit to India, Rubio said that talks were ongoing in Qatar and that the strait of Hormuz would open "one way or another." He acknowledged ongoing discussions about specific language in the initial document.

Trump stated on Truth Social that any deal would either be "great and meaningful, or there will be no deal at all," leaving open the possibility of continued conflict.

The extended negotiations have rippled across the global economy and domestic US politics. Energy bills are rising for millions of people in Britain, with typical household costs increasing by 221 pounds annually due to the impact of the Iran war. In the United States, inflation rose at its fastest pace in three years in April, driven by higher energy prices. Americans have grown increasingly frustrated with Trump's handling of the economic consequences, with his approval rating falling to nearly its lowest level since returning to the White House.

The timing of any announcement remains unclear, with Trump not setting a public deadline for his decision. The Middle East region continues to watch for signals about whether the conflict will continue or whether diplomatic progress can be achieved. Officials across the region are monitoring developments closely as negotiations continue without resolution.

cards.headline: US military disables ship attempting to breach Iran blockade
cards.teaser: The US fired a Hellfire missile into a commercial vessel's engine room in the Gulf of Oman after the ship ignored more than 20 warnings.
cards.body:
US forces disabled another commercial ship trying to breach the naval blockade and reach Iran, according to officials. The military fired a missile into the engine room of the vessel after it ignored more than 20 warnings to stop.

The incident occurred in the Gulf of Oman as part of ongoing enforcement of the blockade. Some ships have been sailing without transponders in an attempt to sneak out of the Strait of Hormuz undetected, though ship transits through the strait have been rising with help from US forces.

cards.headline: Ebola outbreak in DR Congo spreads at unprecedented rate
cards.body:
An outbreak of Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo has spread faster than any previous outbreak on record, with health officials confirming 65 deaths and 246 suspected cases reported so far in Ituri province.

Médecins Sans Frontières has warned that no previous Ebola outbreak has recorded so many cases so soon after its declaration. The statement underscores the severity of the current situation in this central African nation, where the virus has already crossed borders into Uganda.

Uganda's health ministry confirmed an outbreak in the country after a 59-year-old man died in a Kampala hospital following travel from the Democratic Republic of Congo. Officials at the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention expressed concern about the risk of further regional spread.

The World Health Organization estimated the death rate between 30 and 50 percent based on confirmed cases. Anaïs Legand from the WHO's high threat pathogens team said this figure means that up to five out of 10 people are likely to die from the infection.

The outbreak is particularly challenging because the affected Ituri province is a mining hub where thousands of people work in close proximity daily. The constant movement of workers through mining towns makes infectious disease control extremely difficult. Additionally, the region experiences ongoing armed conflict, which has displaced populations into overcrowded camps, further hindering transmission control efforts.

Health authorities identified the virus as the Bundibugyo strain, based on samples detected by the DRC's national research laboratory. This strain is particularly concerning because no licensed vaccine currently exists to prevent it. The Democratic Republic of Congo has experienced 16 Ebola outbreaks since the virus was identified there in 1976, but previous outbreaks typically involved the Zaire strain, for which vaccines are available. Only two previous outbreaks of Bundibugyo virus have been recorded, occurring in 2007 and 2012.

Cases have been reported mainly in the Mongwalu and Rwampara health zones, with suspected cases also appearing in the neighbouring city of Bunia. The Africa CDC convened an urgent meeting with authorities from the Democratic Republic of Congo, Uganda, and South Sudan, along with the World Health Organization and pharmaceutical companies to coordinate response efforts.

Ebola is transmitted through direct contact with body fluids such as blood or vomit from infected people, or from dead bodies during funeral preparations. The virus causes severe hemorrhagic fever and carries a high fatality rate.

The rapid transmission has strained local health infrastructure, which lacks adequate resources to manage the crisis. Aid organizations are working urgently to provide support to medical teams struggling with limited equipment and personnel as the outbreak continues to spread across the region.

cards.headline: Russian drone crashes into Romanian apartment building
cards.teaser: A drone struck an apartment building in eastern Romania, bringing the Russia-Ukraine war into NATO territory.
cards.body:
A Russian drone crashed into an apartment building in eastern Romania on Friday morning, injuring two people. The unmanned aircraft was part of an overnight attack against Ukraine before it veered into NATO territory.

Residents have begun returning to assess damage to their homes in the affected building. The incident has deepened concerns among locals about safety and security, with many expressing anxiety about NATO's ability to defend its members and the broader implications for alliance solidarity against Russian aggression.

cards.headline: Colombia votes in presidential election testing Latin America's left
cards.teaser: Colombians vote in a presidential election pitting a leftist front-runner against a far-right challenger.
cards.body:
Colombia holds a presidential election on Sunday that will test the strength of the left across Latin America. The leftist candidate leads in polls, but faces a far-right outsider who calls himself "The Tiger" and has gained momentum in the race.

The election takes place against a backdrop of resurgent political violence. Ecuador became entangled in the contest when President Daniel Noboa offered to cancel tariffs after speaking with a right-wing presidential candidate, prompting Colombian officials to accuse Ecuador of interfering in the vote.

cards.headline: Ecuador accused of election interference in Colombia
cards.teaser: Ecuador's president offered to cancel tariffs after speaking with a Colombian presidential candidate before the vote.
cards.body:
Ecuadorian President Daniel Noboa offered to cancel tariffs after speaking with a right-wing Colombian presidential candidate shortly before the country's election. Colombian officials accused Ecuador of attempting to influence the electoral process through the tariff proposal.

The incident highlighted concerns about cross-border political interference in the region. Sunday's Colombian presidential vote represented a contest between left and right, with competing visions for addressing the country's decades-long armed conflict.

cards.headline: Trump administration sends conflicting messages on green card policy
cards.teaser: Confusion and anxiety spread among immigrants after the administration issued and then appeared to walk back statements about new green card application requirements.
cards.body:
The Trump administration created confusion about whether most immigrants would need to leave the United States to obtain green cards. The Department of Homeland Security later said that most immigrants would not need to depart the country, contradicting earlier messaging.

A new memo from US Citizenship and Immigration Services suggested that most green card applicants might be forced to apply from abroad. Immigration advocates described the situation as chaotic, while immigrants said the conflicting information from the government was frightening.

cards.headline: Truck crash kills 22 refugees in eastern Afghanistan
cards.teaser: A truck carrying returning refugees crashed in eastern Afghanistan, killing 22 people.
cards.body:
Twenty-two people died when a truck carrying returning refugees crashed in eastern Afghanistan. The vehicle was transporting refugees who were returning to the country.

The crash occurred in the eastern part of Afghanistan. No further information about the cause of the crash or the refugees' origin was provided in initial reports.

cards.headline: Colombia votes in presidential election testing Latin America's left
cards.teaser: Colombians vote in a presidential election pitting a leftist front-runner against a far-right challenger.
cards.body:
Colombia holds a presidential election on Sunday that will test the strength of the left across Latin America. The leftist candidate leads in polls, but faces a far-right outsider who calls himself "The Tiger" and has gained momentum in the race.

The election takes place against a backdrop of resurgent political violence. Ecuador became entangled in the contest when President Daniel Noboa offered to cancel tariffs after speaking with a right-wing presidential candidate, prompting Colombian officials to accuse Ecuador of interfering in the vote.

cards.headline: Iranian soccer team waits for US visas ahead of World Cup
cards.teaser: Iranian soccer players practice in Turkey while awaiting visas to enter the United States for the World Cup.
cards.body:
The Iranian national soccer team is training in Turkey while awaiting visas to enter the United States for the World Cup. The players are preparing for the tournament amid uncertainty about their travel status.

The visa situation has created challenges for the team's preparations, prompting them to develop backup plans as they continue practicing.

cards.headline: Film editor Marcia Lucas dies at 80
cards.teaser: Oscar-winning editor Marcia Lucas, a creative force behind the original Star Wars trilogy, has died.
cards.body:
Marcia Lucas, the Oscar-winning film editor and ex-wife of director George Lucas, has died at age 80. She was widely recognised as a pivotal creative force behind the original Star Wars trilogy.

Lucas's editing work on the space trilogy earned her significant recognition and her contributions were essential to the films' success and lasting cultural impact.

cards.headline: Italy cancels Ye and Travis Scott concerts over security concerns
cards.teaser: Authorities in Italy canceled concerts by Ye and Travis Scott, citing public order and safety.
cards.body:
Kanye West, who now goes by Ye, was scheduled to perform at the Pulse of Gaia festival at RCF Arena in Reggio Emilia on July 18. The city's prefect, Salvatore Angieri, canceled the concert citing "public order and safety issues."

The cancellation followed concerns raised by the local Jewish community regarding West's history of antisemitic remarks. Italian authorities said the decision was made to ensure public safety.

cards.headline: Judge blocks Kennedy Center renovation and renaming
cards.teaser: A federal judge stopped the administration's plans for the Kennedy Center, prompting an angry response from Trump.
cards.body:
A federal judge has blocked the Kennedy Center's planned two-year closure for renovations, at least for now. In a 94-page ruling, the judge stated it was "crystal clear" that the arts complex was named after President John F. Kennedy and cannot wind down its programming to facilitate the renovation project.

The decision represents another legal setback for the administration. Trump responded to the ruling by criticizing the judge and expressing frustration over his recent court losses.

cards.headline: Protesters and supporters clash outside New Jersey ICE facility
cards.teaser: Police responded as opposing groups faced off at a detention center where detainees are on the ninth day of a hunger strike.
cards.body:
Protesters and supporters of ICE operations held competing demonstrations outside Delaney Hall, an immigration detention center in Newark, New Jersey, on Saturday. Counterprotesters wearing Trump hats gathered to support Immigration and Customs Enforcement, while those backing the detained immigrants faced off across police barricades.

The demonstrations came as detainees inside the facility entered the ninth day of a hunger and labor strike, demanding improved conditions and medical care. Senator Cory Booker and Representative Mikie Sherrill both voiced concerns about the detention center's conditions.

cards.headline: Catholic priest convicted of sexual assault in Texas
cards.teaser: A Texas jury found a priest guilty of sexually abusing women under his spiritual care after reporting by The Guardian.
cards.body:
A Catholic priest named Anthony Odiong was convicted in Texas of criminal clergy sexual assault. Prosecutors revealed that he exploited his spiritual authority to pursue sexual contact with devout female parishioners.

Following his conviction on Friday, the Our Lady of Guadalupe healing chapel in Luling, Louisiana—which Odiong had helped build—removed his name from the structure within hours. The names of two women whom he victimized remain inscribed among the chapel's benefactors.

cards.headline: Graham Platner's wife alerted campaign to explicit texts
cards.teaser: The Senate candidate's wife told his campaign about sexually explicit messages he had sent to other women as his race gained momentum.
cards.body:
Graham Platner's wife informed his Senate campaign that he had sent sexually explicit texts to other women, according to multiple reports. The disclosure came as Platner's Senate race was taking off.

The texts with women became a concern for the campaign team after the candidate's wife flagged them. Platner is running for Senate, and the revelations about his communications with other women emerged during the course of his campaign.

hero.headline: Blue Origin rocket explosion damages Florida launch pad
hero.body:
A New Glenn rocket operated by Blue Origin exploded during a test at Cape Canaveral in Florida on Thursday night, threatening NASA's ambitious timeline to build a lunar base and return astronauts to the moon. The explosion occurred during a "hotfire" test at 9 p.m. ET, destroying the launchpad in a massive fireball visible from over 100 miles away.

The incident has serious implications for NASA's Artemis program. Blue Origin had just won a contract on Tuesday to launch the first of three planned missions this year to begin construction of the space agency's $20 billion moon base. The company also competes with SpaceX to provide a lunar lander for the Artemis IV mission scheduled for 2028, which would return astronauts to the lunar surface for the first time since 1972.

Jeff Bezos, Blue Origin's founder, said on social media that all employees were safe and accounted for. He acknowledged the setback while expressing determination to move forward. "It's too early to know the root cause but we're already working to find it," Bezos stated. "Very rough day, but we'll rebuild whatever needs rebuilding and get back to flying."

NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman said the space agency would conduct a full evaluation of its timeline following the explosion. "Spaceflight is unforgiving, and developing new heavy-lift launch capability is extraordinarily difficult," he posted. "We will work with our partners to support a thorough investigation of this anomaly, assess near-term mission impacts, and get back to launching rockets."

The shockwaves from the explosion were felt across Florida's Atlantic coast, with residents in nearby Cape Canaveral and Cocoa Beach reporting that their homes shook. An orange glow was visible as far south as Fort Pierce, 115 miles away, and residents in South Carolina hundreds of miles to the north reported seeing the illuminated sky. Emergency officials confirmed there was no threat from fumes or other hazards, though flames continued burning at the launchpad for more than two hours after the explosion.

The accident marks the latest difficulty for Blue Origin as it competes for government contracts. Last month, a payload from the company's third New Glenn flight ended up in the wrong orbit, leading the Federal Aviation Administration to temporarily ground the rocket. Thursday's test was the first static fire test since the FAA cleared the company to return to flight the previous week.

Elon Musk, CEO of rival SpaceX, commented on the explosion, saying "Most unfortunate" and noting that "Rockets are hard." Both Blue Origin and SpaceX have constructed large new facilities near Cape Canaveral to support crewed and cargo missions with NASA.

cards.headline: United Airlines flight diverted after passenger attempts to breach cockpit
cards.teaser: A United Airlines flight traveling from Chicago to Minneapolis was diverted to Madison, Wisconsin after a passenger attempted to breach the cockpit.
cards.body:
A 75-year-old passenger made multiple attempts to breach the cockpit on a United Airlines flight traveling from Chicago to Minneapolis. The disruptive behavior forced the aircraft to divert to Madison, Wisconsin, where the man was detained.

United Airlines confirmed the incident and the subsequent diversion caused by the passenger's conduct during the flight.

cards.headline: Flight attendant retires after 66 years in the air
cards.teaser: Joan Prince Crandall, the industry's longest-serving flight attendant, is retiring after more than 66 years of flying.
cards.body:
Crandall's retirement ends a career that spanned more than six decades in the airline industry. Her tenure made her the longest-serving flight attendant in the field.

The retirement coincides with International Flight Attendant Day. Airlines including United and Delta marked the occasion by highlighting the work of flight attendants and the skills required for the job.

cards.headline: China's drug development advances draw attention at oncology gathering
cards.teaser: Clinical trials from China are receiving increased attention at an international oncology conference in Chicago as the country's biotechnology industry expands.
cards.body:
China's surging biotechnology industry is drawing attention at an international oncology gathering in Chicago, where clinical trials from the country are being presented. The activity is fueling concern in the United States that American dominance in drug development may be weakening.

The increased prominence of Chinese pharmaceutical research represents a significant shift in the global medical landscape, demonstrating China's expanding capabilities in advancing new treatments through clinical testing.

cards.headline: Freight broker removes carriers based on safety scores after Supreme Court ruling
cards.teaser: C.H. Robinson is removing carriers from its network based on safety scores, a move that may be connected to a recent Supreme Court decision.
cards.body:
C.H. Robinson is removing carriers from its network based on safety scores, a decision that may be linked to a recent Supreme Court ruling. Two weeks prior, the court issued its decision in Montgomery v. Caribe Transport II, which addressed shipper liability questions in freight brokerage cases.

The Supreme Court ruled against expanding shipper liability in the case. This decision, along with separate rulings involving freight brokers and Uber in injury law matters, was characterized as significant losses for those companies. C.H. Robinson's carrier removal strategy appears to reflect the legal landscape shaped by these rulings.

cards.headline: SpaceX initial public offering raises concerns for retail investors
cards.teaser: The anticipated SpaceX IPO has drawn warnings from analysts about prospects for ordinary investors buying shares at the expected valuation.
cards.body:
Companies valued as highly as SpaceX, OpenAI, and Anthropic have historically provided poor returns for retail investors who buy shares after an initial public offering. One analyst issued a harsh recommendation for investors to avoid the SpaceX IPO entirely.

For Wall Street, the situation presents a dilemma. Missing out on a major offering like SpaceX carries risks, but so does participating if the company underperforms after going public. The IPO structure may benefit company insiders and early investors more than those who purchase shares on the public market.

cards.headline: French manufacturer uses AI to boost productivity without cutting workers
cards.teaser: Schneider Electric implemented artificial intelligence in its manufacturing operations to increase worker productivity rather than eliminate jobs.
cards.body:
I'm returning the original card text unchanged.

The two additional sources provided are about different stories — one covers concerns about AI-generated code quality among software developers, and the other discusses Ukraine's use of AI drones in military operations. Neither source contains information about Schneider Electric or the French manufacturer's approach to using AI to boost productivity without workforce reductions.

Original card text:

The French multinational company chose to deploy AI technology as a tool to make its existing workforce more productive. The approach differs from how many companies have used automation and AI, which often leads to workforce reductions.

Schneider Electric's strategy involved integrating AI into manufacturing processes in ways that augment what workers do rather than replace them. The company's decision represents an alternative path for how businesses can adopt new technology while maintaining employment levels.

hero.headline: Microsoft threatens legal action against security researcher over exploit disclosure
hero.body:
Microsoft has threatened legal action against a security researcher over the public disclosure of software exploits. The researcher, who operates under the pseudonym Nightmare-Eclipse, publicly released proof-of-concept code for six zero-day vulnerabilities without providing Microsoft advance notice.

Zero-day vulnerabilities are security flaws unknown to software makers with no available patch. Public disclosure of such vulnerabilities before fixes are developed leaves systems vulnerable to attack.

Microsoft characterized the disclosures as uncoordinated, meaning they lacked the advance notice and development time the company typically expects. The approach has drawn criticism from the security community, with observers calling it heavy-handed. The researcher has stated feeling humiliated by Microsoft's response and pledged what was described as a significant retaliation.

Microsoft involved law enforcement in the matter, with some reports suggesting the company has threatened criminal investigation. This escalation has drawn particular scrutiny, especially since Microsoft has not publicly detailed what legal violations it believes occurred.

The incident has reignited debate within the cybersecurity community about proper vulnerability disclosure practices. Security researchers who discover flaws in widely used software face a choice: report them privately to the company, disclose them publicly, or sell the information on the dark market.

Coordinated disclosure has become the industry standard, where researchers give companies time to develop and release patches before public disclosure. This approach aims to balance protecting users with allowing companies adequate time to respond. However, some researchers argue that companies sometimes move too slowly on privately reported vulnerabilities or release inadequate fixes.

The tension between large technology companies and independent security researchers reflects deeper challenges in the cybersecurity ecosystem. While companies understandably want time to address vulnerabilities before they become public knowledge, researchers sometimes grow frustrated with slow response times or feel their concerns are not taken seriously.

The researcher's use of a pseudonym complicates any potential legal action Microsoft might pursue. Some sources suggest the researcher may be a disgruntled former employee, though this remains unconfirmed.

Technology news outlets have highlighted the conflict between Microsoft and the researcher, framing it as emblematic of ongoing disputes in the industry. The situation underscores the delicate relationship between major software vendors and the independent security researchers who help identify and expose flaws in their products.

The outcome of this case could influence how both companies and researchers approach vulnerability disclosure in the future, potentially affecting the speed at which critical security flaws are addressed and made public.

cards.headline: Nvidia-powered Windows PCs set to launch next week
cards.teaser: The first Windows computers running on Nvidia processors will be unveiled at an upcoming event.
cards.body:
Nvidia is preparing to launch its first processors designed for Windows laptops. The new chips will be unveiled at the company's GTC event next week.

Nvidia, Microsoft, and Arm have posted cryptic messages on social media ahead of the announcement. This marks Nvidia's entry into the laptop processor market, expanding beyond its traditional focus on graphics cards.

cards.headline: Google launches Gemini Spark AI assistant for Ultra subscribers
cards.teaser: Google has released a 24/7 AI assistant called Gemini Spark that automates everyday tasks.
cards.body:
Google has rolled out Gemini Spark, a persistent AI assistant available to Google AI Ultra subscribers in the United States. Unlike traditional AI tools that respond to individual queries, Spark runs continuously to help automate everyday tasks. The assistant can summarize emails in your inbox and assist with planning local events.

Early reviews have found the tool genuinely useful for daily automation. However, observers have questioned Google's decision to launch Spark as a standalone product rather than integrating its capabilities directly into existing Google services.

cards.headline: GitHub Copilot switches to token-based billing
cards.teaser: Microsoft's GitHub Copilot has changed its pricing model, drawing complaints from developers.
cards.body:
GitHub Copilot has moved from its previous pricing structure to a token-based billing system. The change has generated criticism among developers who use the AI coding assistant.

The new billing approach charges users based on the number of tokens processed, similar to how many AI services price their offerings. Some observers have characterized the shift as marking the end of a favorable period for Copilot users.

cards.headline: Former Snap employees launch Ghost Angels investment fund
cards.teaser: A group of 20 former Snap employees has created a fund to invest in social media companies.
cards.body:
Twenty former Snap employees have launched Ghost Angels, an investment fund dedicated to backing the next generation of social media startups. The group of alumni is pooling their resources and expertise to support new ventures in the social media space.

This move reflects a broader pattern of experienced technologists from established companies creating their own investment vehicles to nurture emerging startups in sectors where they have deep knowledge and networks.

cards.headline: Meta working on AI-powered pendant device
cards.teaser: Meta is developing a wearable AI device in the form of a pendant.
cards.body:
Meta is building an AI pendant as part of its expanding hardware efforts. The device represents another bet by the company on AI-integrated consumer electronics.

The pendant would join Meta's existing hardware lineup, which includes virtual reality headsets and smart glasses. The company has been investing heavily in AI capabilities across its product range.

cards.headline: Venture capitalists discuss AI investment trends
cards.teaser: Three prominent venture capitalists shared their views on the current state of AI startup funding.
cards.body:
Top venture capitalists discussed what they see as groupthink in AI investing during a recent conversation. One investor joked that 22-year-olds building AI products in San Francisco might already have seed funding offers, while 19-year-olds could be receiving Series A term sheets.

The comments highlight the intensity of competition among investors to back AI startups. The conversation touched on concerns about whether enthusiasm for AI investments has led to inflated valuations and reduced scrutiny of business fundamentals.

hero.headline: PSG retain Champions League title with penalty shootout win over Arsenal
hero.body:
Paris Saint-Germain won their second consecutive Champions League title after defeating Arsenal in a penalty shootout in Budapest. The match remained goalless through regular time before Arsenal took the lead in the second half, only for PSG to equalize and force the contest to extra time and penalties.

Kai Havertz gave Arsenal an early advantage in the second half with a well-taken finish from a tight angle on the left side of the box. His shot found the top corner after he reacted quicker than PSG's defenders to a charging run from Leandro Trossard. The goal appeared to put Arsenal on course for their first Champions League title, which would have completed a historic season following their Premier League triumph.

PSG responded with characteristic patience, eventually finding their breakthrough when Ousmane Dembele equalized from the penalty spot in the 65th minute after Khvicha Kvaratskhelia was fouled by Cristhian Mosquera. Neither side could find a winner in regular time or extra time, setting up a dramatic penalty shootout.

The shootout proved decisive when Arsenal's Eberechi Eze missed in the second round after a stuttering run, while Gabriel Magalhaes faced the deciding kick in the fifth round with everything on the line. Gabriel appeared to rush his approach, and referee Daniel Siebert delayed him slightly, adding to the pressure. The defender went for power but his shot sailed over the crossbar, handing PSG victory.

Arsenal's defensive organization had been exemplary throughout the match under Mikel Arteta's tactical plan. The London club prioritized solidity and compression of space, with standout performances from Gabriel, who made numerous tackles, and midfielder Myles Lewis-Skelly. Arsenal's transitions caused PSG problems, though the French side dominated possession without creating clear-cut opportunities in the first half.

PSG's patience eventually paid off when they worked their patterns to create the penalty that led to their equalizer. Luis Enrique's team showed resilience after falling behind, maintaining their attacking threat while Arsenal made bold substitutions including bringing on Viktor Gyokeres for Martin Odegaard.

The defeat represents heartbreak for Arsenal after they came so close to achieving an unprecedented domestic and European double. Their Premier League success earlier in the month had been their first league title in 22 years, and a Champions League triumph would have cemented one of the greatest seasons in the club's history.

PSG's back-to-back titles establish them among European football's most successful dynasties. The French club has now demonstrated sustained success in continental competition under Enrique's management, validating their substantial investment in top talent and establishing a standard that rivals the greatest eras in European club football.

cards.headline: Defending champion Coco Gauff eliminated from French Open in third round
cards.teaser: American tennis player Coco Gauff lost her third-round match at the French Open to Anastasia Potapova.
cards.body:
Coco Gauff's bid to defend her French Open title ended in the third round with a loss to Anastasia Potapova. The 28th seed defeated Gauff 4-6, 7-6 (1), 6-4 in a competitive match at Roland Garros.

Potapova proved to be a formidable opponent, matching Gauff's court coverage during long baseline rallies. The upset victory removes the defending champion from the tournament and sends Potapova through to the next round.

cards.headline: Vegas Golden Knights and Carolina Hurricanes to meet in 2026 Stanley Cup Final
cards.teaser: The NHL announced ticket sales details for the Stanley Cup Final between the Vegas Golden Knights and Carolina Hurricanes.
cards.body:
The Carolina Hurricanes have reached the Stanley Cup Final for the first time in 20 years, breaking through their Eastern Conference final barrier after eight years of attempts. Rod Brind'Amour's team will face the Vegas Golden Knights in the championship series.

The Hurricanes will host Games 1 and 2 before the series moves to Vegas. The Golden Knights have announced ticket sales information for their home games in the Final.

cards.headline: White Sox place Munetaka Murakami on injured list with hamstring strain
cards.teaser: Chicago White Sox slugger Munetaka Murakami will miss four to six weeks with a Grade 2 hamstring strain.
cards.body:
The Chicago White Sox placed outfielder Munetaka Murakami on the injured list after he suffered a right hamstring strain. Medical imaging revealed a Grade 2 strain that will sideline him for four to six weeks.

Murakami exited a recent game with hamstring tightness before undergoing further evaluation. The White Sox called up Jacob Gonzalez from the minor leagues to fill the roster spot. Murakami had been a key contributor to the White Sox lineup before the injury.

cards.headline: Scotland midfielder Billy Gilmour ruled out of World Cup with knee injury
cards.teaser: Billy Gilmour suffered a knee injury during Scotland's friendly win over Curacao and will miss the World Cup.
cards.body:
Scotland midfielder Billy Gilmour has been ruled out of the World Cup after sustaining a knee injury during Saturday's 4-1 friendly victory over Curaçao.

Despite Scotland's strong second-half performance—which included playing against 10 men for over half the match—the injury dampened the optimism ahead of the tournament. Gilmour's absence leaves a significant gap in Scotland's midfield as they prepare for their first World Cup appearance in 28 years. Manchester United's Fletcher has been mentioned as a potential replacement on the squad roster.

cards.headline: Northampton Saints secure home playoff semifinal with win over Gloucester
cards.teaser: George Furbank scored a last-minute try to give Northampton Saints victory over Gloucester in an 11-try match.
cards.body:
Northampton Saints defeated Gloucester in a thrilling encounter that produced 11 tries across both teams. George Furbank scored a dramatic late try to seal victory for the Saints.

The win guarantees Northampton will host a semifinal match in the Premiership playoffs, with Furbank's last-gasp effort proving decisive in an entertaining back-and-forth contest.

cards.headline: New Zealand add Mitchell Santner to Test squad for England series
cards.teaser: All-rounder Mitchell Santner returns to New Zealand's Test squad ahead of the series against England starting at Lord's.
cards.body:
New Zealand have recalled all-rounder Mitchell Santner for the Test series against England, which begins at Lord's on Thursday. His return is seen as a significant boost to the team's prospects.

Santner's inclusion strengthens New Zealand's squad with a player capable of contributing with both bat and ball across the multi-match series.

hero.headline: Oscar-Winning Star Wars Editor Marcia Lucas Dies at 80
hero.body:
Marcia Lucas, the Oscar-winning film editor whose work on the original Star Wars helped shape one of cinema's most influential franchises, has died at age 80.

Lucas won the Academy Award for Best Film Editing for Star Wars in 1978. Her editing work on the original trilogy proved instrumental in crafting the pacing and structure that made the films cultural landmarks. She also edited other major films of the era, including American Graffiti and Taxi Driver.

Lucasfilm released a tribute following news of her death. Lucas was married to Star Wars creator George Lucas from 1969 to 1983, a period that encompassed the creation and release of the original Star Wars trilogy.

Her editing contributions extended beyond the technical aspects of filmmaking. Industry professionals have long credited her with shaping key narrative decisions in the original Star Wars, helping transform raw footage into a cohesive story that resonated with audiences worldwide.

Lucas worked during an era when film editing was undergoing significant technological changes. Her career spanned the transition from traditional cutting techniques to more modern approaches, and her work on Star Wars demonstrated how editing could elevate science fiction filmmaking.

After her divorce from George Lucas, she stepped away from the film industry. Despite her reduced public profile in later decades, her influence on cinema remained substantial. Film scholars and editors continue to study her work on the original Star Wars trilogy as an example of how editing shapes storytelling.

The original Star Wars film, released in 1977, became a cultural phenomenon that spawned a multi-billion dollar franchise spanning films, television series, books, and merchandise. The editing work that helped make that first film successful earned recognition from the Academy and from peers in the film industry.

Lucas leaves behind a legacy as one of the most important editors in American cinema history. Her work demonstrated how editing serves as a fundamental storytelling tool, particularly in the science fiction and adventure genres that dominated Hollywood in the late 1970s and early 1980s.

cards.headline: Actress Kelly Curtis, Sister of Jamie Lee Curtis, Dies at 69
cards.teaser: Kelly Curtis, who appeared in films including The Sentinel, died at her home.
cards.body:
Kelly Curtis, an American actress and the older sister of Jamie Lee Curtis, died at age 69. Jamie Lee Curtis announced her sister's death in a Facebook post, writing that Kelly passed away at her home.

Kelly Curtis appeared in several films during her career, including The Sentinel. Jamie Lee Curtis described her sister's death as peaceful, noting she died in nature. The Facebook post included a warm tribute to Kelly Lee Curtis.

cards.headline: Artists Pull Out of Government-Sponsored Freedom 250 Concerts in Washington
cards.teaser: Multiple performers have withdrawn from planned appearances at Freedom 250 events.
cards.body:
Several artists have withdrawn from government-sponsored Freedom 250 concerts in Washington, including Martina McBride, Bret Michaels, and Young MC. Some performers expressed concerns that the event would be political in nature.

President Trump responded on his Truth Social account Saturday with a series of posts attacking the departing performers as "third rate artists." He announced plans to hold an "America Is Back" rally on Wednesday to replace the concert series, suggesting it would feature a performer with a larger audience than Elvis and that only "great patriots" would be invited.

cards.headline: San Antonio Spurs Force Game 7 Against Thunder in Western Conference Final
cards.teaser: Victor Wembanyama scored 28 points as the Spurs routed Oklahoma City to set up a deciding game.
cards.body:
The San Antonio Spurs defeated the Oklahoma City Thunder 118-91 in Game 6 of the NBA Western Conference Final, forcing a winner-take-all Game 7. Victor Wembanyama led the Spurs with 28 points in the victory.

The dominant performance came after the teams had split the first five games of the series. Game 7 will determine which team advances to the NBA Finals. The Spurs' 27-point margin of victory represented their largest win of the playoff series against Oklahoma City.

cards.headline: Tom Holland Expresses Interest in Mentoring Future Spider-Man Actor
cards.teaser: The current Spider-Man star told Empire magazine he wants to help set up the next actor in the franchise.
cards.body:
Tom Holland said he looks forward to passing the Spider-Man role to the next actor who takes over the Marvel franchise. Speaking to Empire magazine, Holland said he would like to help set up whoever plays the next iteration of the character, whether that is Miles Morales, Spider-Gwen, Spider-Woman, or another version.

Holland compared his potential future role to what Robert Downey Jr. did for him when he joined the Marvel Cinematic Universe. The actor indicated he wants to provide similar mentorship and support to help establish the next Spider-Man star in the franchise.

cards.headline: Paris Saint-Germain Wins Second Consecutive UEFA Champions League Title
cards.teaser: The French club defeated Arsenal 4-3 on penalty kicks to claim back-to-back European championships.
cards.body:
Paris Saint-Germain retained the UEFA Champions League title by defeating Arsenal on penalty kicks in a tense final. Eberechi Eze and Gabriel missed crucial penalties for Arsenal, ultimately handing PSG victory and establishing them as a dominant European force with back-to-back championships.

For Arsenal, the loss dashed hopes of completing an historic season. The club had just won the Premier League for the first time in 22 years, ending a drought that began with their famous Invincibles team in 2004. Manager Mikel Arteta's side came close to achieving what would have been their greatest season ever, but fell short on European soccer's biggest stage.

cards.headline: Actor Kirk Cameron Says He Left California for Tennessee
cards.teaser: The Growing Pains star cited politics and family concerns in explaining his move.
cards.body:
Kirk Cameron, best known for his role on Growing Pains, explained on the Adam Carolla Podcast why he relocated from California to Tennessee. Cameron cited the state's "terrible politics" and other factors that he felt made it challenging to raise a family there.

While Cameron emphasized that California has benefits for families with significant financial resources, he ultimately decided to move away from the state where he grew up. He did not elaborate on the specific policies or conditions that influenced his decision.

hero.headline: Trump criticizes court system after rulings against tariff policy and Kennedy Center renaming
hero.teaser: President Trump called the U.S. court system rigged after recent decisions blocked economic policy measures and the addition of his name to the Kennedy Center.
hero.body:
President Trump criticized the U.S. court system as "rigged" following recent judicial decisions against his administration. A judge ruled that Trump's name must be removed from the Kennedy Center, determining in a 94-page decision that the arts complex was clearly named for President John F. Kennedy. The court also blocked the center from closing for two years of planned renovations.

The criticism followed court rulings that blocked key elements of Trump's economic agenda, including measures related to tariff policy. Trump expressed his frustration through a post on Truth Social, comparing the court system to other institutions he has previously criticized.

cards.headline: Trump plans rally for July 4 after entertainers withdraw from America 250 celebration
cards.teaser: President Trump announced he will hold a political rally to mark the nation's 250th anniversary after several artists pulled out of the Great American State Fair.
cards.body:
President Trump announced plans to hold a political rally on July 4th to celebrate America's 250th anniversary after several entertainers withdrew from the Great American State Fair event scheduled for the National Mall that week. Performers including Young MC, Bret Michaels and Martina McBride cited concerns that the event would become political.

Trump responded to the artist withdrawals by framing his rally as an alternative way to mark the milestone anniversary. He suggested the performers were hesitant about appearing at the state fair event.

cards.headline: White House denies report that Wiles advised Vance to reduce social media use
cards.teaser: The White House rejected a New York Times report claiming Chief of Staff Susie Wiles suggested Vice President Vance take a break from social media.
cards.body:
The White House rejected a New York Times report claiming Chief of Staff Susie Wiles advised Vice President Vance to step back from social media. White House Communications Director Steven Cheung dismissed the story as "complete fake news" on X.

Cheung's denial came the same day the Times published its account of the alleged guidance from Wiles to the vice president.

cards.headline: Defense Secretary Hegseth softens China rhetoric while urging allies to share security burden
cards.teaser: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth moderated his criticism of China during remarks to Pacific leaders, weeks after President Trump met with Chinese officials in Beijing.
cards.body:
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth struck a more measured tone on China while addressing Pacific leaders at a security summit in Singapore. His comments represented a shift from previous harder-line rhetoric, coming weeks after President Trump met with Chinese officials in Beijing. Notably, Hegseth sidestepped discussing Taiwan during his remarks.

Hegseth urged Asian allies to increase their military spending and share more responsibility for regional security. He acknowledged "rightful alarm" about China's military expansion while maintaining a moderate stance on U.S.-China relations. The defense secretary also addressed concerns about American commitment to the region, including future arms deals with allies.

cards.headline: Rep. Mace says no regrets on Epstein files vote despite Trump endorsing primary opponent
cards.teaser: Rep. Nancy Mace said she does not regret voting to release Jeffrey Epstein files even after President Trump endorsed her challenger in the South Carolina governor's race.
cards.body:
Rep. Nancy Mace said she stands by her decision to push for the release of files related to convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein. The South Carolina congresswoman made the statement after President Trump endorsed her challenger in the Republican primary for governor.

Mace, who is running in the GOP primary for the state's top office, declared "I voted to release the Epstein files. NO REGRETS" in response to Trump's endorsement of her rival candidate.

cards.headline: Giants quarterback Dart defends Trump rally appearance as act of patriotism
cards.teaser: New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart said he introduced President Trump at a rally out of patriotism, not partisanship, after facing criticism for the appearance.
cards.body:
New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart defended his recent appearance at a New York rally where he introduced President Trump. Dart said he acted out of patriotism rather than political motivation.

Dart described the opportunity to introduce the president as unique. He said his thinking was simple when deciding whether to participate in the event, framing the decision as about love of country rather than partisan politics.
